To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have designed and prototyped a hardware accelerator for homomorphic encryption that improves the performance and practicality of lattice-based schemes, such as LTV, and that it can be integrated into a larger homomorphic encryption co-processor.
our hardware accelerator is capable of performing the CRT and iCRIT operations 2.7x faster than a state-of-the-art software reference implementation, with an average power consumption of 3.8 Watts.

1) We design and implement an FPGA-based accelerator for the CRT and i CRT lattice primitives, and 2) we show that our accelerator can speed up the performance of the LTV scheme by a factor of 2.3x-3.7x.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the practicality of using homomorphic encryption in the cloud.
the practical implementation of a homomorphic encryption co-processor.
the design of an FPGA-based accelerator to support the practical use of homomorphic encryption.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the performance of the accelerator is comparable to the software reference implementation.

the performance of our accelerator is competitive with software implementations of CRT/iCRT on a modern multicore CPU and is a significant improvement over a software implementation of the same functionality on a single core CPU.
our FPGA-based CRT and iCRT accelerator can speed up the performance of NTRU LTV by 3-5x, and the performance of the encrypted string comparison by 2-3x.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are able to achieve a 3.5x speedup in the iCRT computation, and 1.7x speedup in string comparison, over the software reference implementation.

we have demonstrated a practical hardware accelerator for lattice-based homomorphic encryption schemes that can be integrated with existing software implementations to provide a performance boost of over 1000x for the CRT/iCRT operations.
we have demonstrated a 10x speedup in the performance of the CRT and 3.5x speedup in string comparison over a state-of-the-art software implementation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can improve the performance of homomorphic encryption schemes by 10 to 1000x by offloading these computations to a hardware accelerator.
we can achieve up to 100x speedup for the CRT and iRCT operations, and up to 10x speedup for ring addition, subtraction and multiplication.
the CRT/iCRT bottlenecks of homomorphic encryption can be efficiently accelerated by FPGA hardware, and that this hardware can be used as a co-processor to a host computer.
